headline: Microsoft president Brad Smith warned the White House that restricting green cards for skilled foreign workers could harm US technology for a generation.
score_reason: A senior executive of a company directly hit by the action responds to the Vance accusations; one side of a dispute, though the White House action is documented.
importance_line: Skilled foreign workers at the eight suspended employers, and the US tech sector's ability to hire talent, are affected, but Microsoft's figures are its own and the White House has not yet answered them.
summary: Politico reports, as relayed by Newsweek and The Indian Express, that Brad Smith, vice chair and president of Microsoft, said in an interview on Wednesday that blocking green-card routes for highly skilled immigrants could cripple US tech for more than a generation, and called Vice President JD Vance's accusation that Microsoft replaced laid-off Americans with foreign workers "completely off base". This is Smith's reply to Vance's 8 Oct 2026 press conference, where Vance said Microsoft laid off 6,000 US workers while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B visas and almost 3,000 green cards; Smith said Microsoft hired 9,200 American workers last fiscal year.
notes: Politico blocked (403); read Newsweek and The Indian Express reports of the Politico interview. Interview Wed 14 Oct in Ireland. Reply story: Vance's 8 Oct press conference named; not checked whether we ran it earlier.
